newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik warlord leaves centre of disputed town.
newsitem.headline: Tajik warlord leaves centre of disputed town.

text.p: Tanks and most troops of the mutinous commander of the Tajik government's elite armoured brigade left the centre of Tursunzade in western Tajikistan on Friday but it was not clear whether the unit had returned to barracks.

Reuters correspondent Chris Bird saw no tanks or other armour and there was only a handful of troops at the town's centre where the rebel brigade commander, Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, and his men were based on Thursday.

Khudoyberdyev, who led an armed rebellion against the government in February last year, sent his brigade into Tursunzade, an aluminium-producing town 45 km (30 miles) west of the capital Dushanbe, to unseat a local strongman.
Embattled Tajik President Imamali Rakhmonov ordered the commander back to barracks, saying Khudoyberdyev's action was "illegal".
A local official said Khudoyberdyev's forces had left for the town of Kurgan-Tyube but rumours circulated in Tursunzade that the commander had hidden his tanks inside a sprawling aluminium plant.
A senior plant official said the smelter was still operating at 40-45 percent of its 500,000 tonnes per year capacity.
